system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production software or data services
G2: cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure, BigQuery)
G3: Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka
G4: data modelling or schema design
G5: Docker beyond a tutorial
G6: CI/CD
G7: automated testing of code
G8: REST APIs in production
G9: PLC programming
G10: data engineering certification

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Upgrading Python/MATLAB scripts to 'production Python services' or 'built and deployed data pipelines'
T2: Describing the Task Scheduler script as an orchestrated ETL pipeline or adding Airflow/dbt
T3: Claiming he designed or administered the SQL Server database or did data modelling
T4: Listing GCP, BigQuery, Docker, CI/CD or Kafka because the ad asks for them
T5: Presenting the laptop Flask API or the Docker Compose tutorial as professional backend work
T6: Calling him a PLC programmer or industrial automation engineer
T7: Listing the unfinished online course as a certificate
T8: Retitling his current job as Data Engineer or Software Engineer, or presenting him as a senior data engineer because of 12 years of engineering
T9: Old cover letter is addressed to his current employer and says he works at Halvik Pumps

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL & Test Data
Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 |
linkedin.com/in/tfl-example
Professional Summary
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design and test and validation of
automotive and industrial components. Develops Python tools to process test-rig data, check channels
against specifications and generate reports, including a nightly workflow handling approximately 2
GB of data per week across six rigs. Experience querying SQL Server, writing results to an IT-created
staging table and creating Power BI reporting for engineering users. Currently transitioning toward
data engineering and completing an online data engineering course.
Experience
Test & Validation Engineer, Corvane Automotive Components — Setúbal Mar
2019–Present
• Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across six
servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; write reports sent to OEM customers.
• Developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and npTDMS to parse TDMS and
CSV rig output, check channels against test specifications and generate standard report figures;
reduced report preparation from approximately three days to half a day per test.
• Run the processing workflow nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler; it writes
summary results to an IT-created staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database. Packaged as
an internal tool now used by four other test engineers.
• Query the main test-results database in SQL Server for trend analysis across three product
generations; the queries are read-only.
• Created a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to
failure by product generation; used by approximately 15 validation and design engineers.
• Correlate rig results with ANSYS Mechanical FEA and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures;
proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that cut warranty returns for that part by 40%.
• Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive used to select rig load profiles.
• Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).
Mechanical Design Engineer, Halvik Pumps — Porto Sep 2014–Feb 2019
• Designed centrifugal pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and prepared production drawings
with GD&T; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
• Performed structural FEA of casings in ANSYS; supported a change from grey cast iron to ductile
iron for one casing family, saving 12% in material cost.
• Supported conversion of the pump performance test bench to a Siemens S7 PLC-controlled setup,
adjusting setpoints and timers in TIA Portal under the automation engineer’s supervision.
• Wrote a LabVIEW acquisition program for the performance test bench, reducing test setup time
from approximately two hours to 30 minutes.
Selected Project
Bike-sharing trips API | Personal learning project, 2025
• Built a small Flask API with three read-only endpoints over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded
into SQLite. Runs on a personal laptop; followed a tutorial to run it with Docker Compose. Used
Python, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose and Git.
Education
MSc Mechanical Engineering, Sado Valley Polytechnic 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading
Professional Development
Online Data Engineering course — in progress; six of nine modules completed.
Skills
Data processing and reporting: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server,
SQL, Power BI, Excel/VBA
Engineering and testing: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5,
LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Personal learning project tools: Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git
Languages
Portuguese (native), English (fluent), Spanish (good)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Halden Pay Data Platform Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. My background
combines 12 years in mechanical engineering with hands-on development of Python tools that
turn test data into reliable reports and engineering decisions. I am now moving toward data
engineering, and the team’s focus on reusable platform capabilities is closely aligned with that
direction.
At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed a Python workflow that parses
approximately 2 GB of TDMS and CSV data per week from six test rigs, checks channels
against test specifications and generates report figures. It runs nightly on a lab PC, writes
summary results to a staging table in SQL Server, and is used by four other test engineers. I
also built a Power BI dashboard from that table for around 15 validation and design
engineers. These projects reduced report preparation from approximately three days to half a
day per test and made test-result trends easier for colleagues to use.
My experience is with practical internal data-processing workflows rather than a cloud data
platform: the scripts run on a lab PC, and IT created the SQL Server staging table. I am
currently completing an online data engineering course, with six of nine modules completed. I
would bring a strong foundation in Python-based data processing, SQL querying, test-data
quality checks and collaboration with engineering and BI users, while continuing to develop my
data engineering experience. I am happy to commute to Lisbon for the hybrid arrangement.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and transition into data
engineering could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team. Thank you for your
consideration.
Best regards, Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
